title: The Bone Flowers
summary: Followers of the Song of the Shadow.

claims.text: Masters of the emotionless Cold Mind, the Bone Flowers have served Korea's Green Courts, the uji of Japan and the Five August Courts, destroying some Kin-jin and shielding others.

Apart from those who give themselves wholly to study, they keep their old roles as they wait for the Age of Sorrow: learning from other Dharmas, dealing with the dead and spirits, and practising stealth, spying and assassination.
Followers share the Dharma's beliefs and little else; they may differ in sex, origin and much more.

title: Bone Flowers in Hong Kong
summary: The Shadow's century of peace with the gweilo, and its end.

claims.text: For a century the Bone Flowers handled the Western factions of shen in Hong Kong, and dealings with the Kin-jin grew almost easy.
That uneasy peace fell apart in 1997, when the Quincunx resolved to seize Hong Kong from the Kin-jin by force.

title: The Senryo
summary: The occupation of the Japanese Yin World.

claims.text: Local shen call the Japanese Yin World's state the Senryo: it is in effect under foreign occupation by the Chinese Yellow Springs.
Bone Flower gaki have often tried to help Japanese ghosts get free, and the recent turmoil in the Yin World looks like a chance to release the ghosts of the ancestors.

title: Bishamon Bone Flowers
summary: Shadow followers of the traditionalist Japanese house.

claims.text: Bone Flowers of House Bishamon, like many of their uji, prefer the wilderness; in one region where cold Yin gathers, the Yin dragon lines are strong and clean, and the long winter nights leave them free to travel, study and hold long rites.

title: The Eight Sacred Steps
summary: An old, well-known wu of the Bone Court.

claims.text: Bone Flower histories tell of three great wu made only of Shadow followers, still heroes to Kuei-jin, as well as wu whose stories serve as warnings.

Only one of the Eight Sacred Steps followed a different Dharma: Chun Quan, a Devil-Tiger. They took their Second Breaths in Chongqing, learned the Bone Court's ways and brought back most of the relics found near Meru that the great Bone Court now holds.
